divOfScalarTimesVector/1a-divPerp/twoGau.cause: Expected property of the scheme, not a bug: Div(f) holds a (1/J) d(J f_x)/dx term; at the first cell next to the axis the 1/J (x = dx/2) multiplies the second-order error of the centred derivative, so the error of that cell falls as dx. Away from the axis (x >= 1) the order is 2, reproduced in a Python replica of the stencil.

divOfScalarTimesVector/2a-divSource/twoG.cause: Expected property of the scheme, not a bug: div_f_GradPerp_g holds an (f/J) DDX(g) term; at the cells next to the axis (x = (i + 1/2) dx) the 1/J multiplies the second-order error of the centred derivative, so the error at a fixed cell index falls as dx. Here f is nonzero at the axis; in twoGaussians it vanishes there, which is why that input converges at 2. Checked in a Python replica of the stencil that reproduces the CI errors (1.23e-4, 6.00e-5, 2.96e-5): the (f/J) DDX(g) term carries almost all of the error, both fields continue exactly through the axis (the guard cell is exact), and the error at x >= 1 or x >= 3 converges at 2. JTimesDivSource multiplies by J, removes the 1/J, and converges at 2 with the same inputs.
